text:
perf-bench-bot: ALERT: perf/regression detected in nightly CI job `small-batch` (suite: small-batch-quant-2). p50 +135% vs baseline. Details + artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/1987654321/small-batch.tar.gz
```
SMALL-BATCH SUMMARY
metric      baseline   current    delta
p50         12.1ms     28.4ms     +135%
p95         48.0ms     95.7ms     +99%
throughput  850/s      430/s      -49%
```
Maria: cc @Ben @Taylor @Sami seeing this first thing. Any idea if we changed small-seq kernel paths or batch scheduler overnight?
Ben: oncall here, I'll take a look. Kicking off a local repro and grabbing artifacts. @perf-bench-bot can you paste the direct CI job URL + flamegraphs?
perf-bench-bot: Job URL: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/1987654321
Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/1987654321/small-batch.tar.gz
Flamegraph: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/1987654321/flame.svg
Taylor: I'll diff baseline commit -> current. My first guess is the scheduler PR that tweaked kernel selection heuristics (PR #2871). Starting a quick bisect.
Sami: I have a hunch it's influenced by the infra CUDA upgrade we rolled to dedicated pools yesterday (CUDA 12.3). That can flip kernel picks for short-seq attention. Can someone repro pinned to cuda11? I can spin a node if needed.
Maria: Good call. If throughput dropped ~50% it's probably a fallback kernel. Ben, can you grab the runtime logs and search for "selected_kernel" or similar?
Ben: Quick grep from runner logs:
```
[2026-11-03T03:12:15Z] model: gpt-small | seq_len:8 | using_kernel: attn_v2_smallseq_fallback
[2026-11-03T03:12:15Z] selected_kernel_hint: fast_attn_v1 not available for device arch sm90
[2026-11-03T03:12:16Z] kv_cache_alloc: ok
```
Ben: uploading flame and a short perf snapshot to CI (linked above). Top of flame: attention_forward_kernel_shortseq / attn_v2_smallseq_fallback.
Taylor: If fallback is being selected we lose the hand-optimized path. I just checked PR #2871 — we removed the small-seq fast path for a memory correctness fix. That could explain the regression. I'll prepare a revert PR for canary.
Maria: Please open the revert and tag it emergency. Also add a canary job pinned to the pre-PR commit. We need fast verification before rolling the fix back to main infra. :eyes:
Ben: Creating canary run now. Command I used locally: `./scripts/bench-run --suite small-batch --commit <revert-commit> --device cuda11`
perf-bench-bot: Canary queued: ci/canary/small-batch-revert/1987654421. Will post results when done.
Taylor: Thanks. Also add the small-batch p50/p95/throughput checks to the rollback checklist (so future reverts run the same assertions).
Sami: I'll reach out to infra to pause additional CUDA upgrades on dedicated pools until we verify canary. If revert fixes perf we can coordinate a follow-up fix to keep correctness while restoring fast path.
Maria: Sounds good. Next steps: Ben watches canary, Taylor opens revert PR + tests, Sami holds infra upgrades. Keep updates here. If the canary passes we'll schedule emergency rollback and cherry-pick a permanent fix.
Ben: ETA for canary results ~25m. Will post logs here when complete.
Taylor: Opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2920 (revert small-seq removal).
Sami: Noted — holding upgrades and notified infra on pager.
perf-bench-bot: Update: canary finished (1987654521). Summary: p50 13.0ms, p95 49.2ms, throughput 830/s — within tolerance vs baseline. Full artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/1987654521/canary-compare.json
Maria: Great — looks like revert fixed it. Ben/Taylor, please follow rollback runbook and schedule emergency revert to main. Also capture a short postmortem summary after rollback. :white_check_mark:
Ben: Starting rollback per runbook. Will post deployment window and confirmation when done.
Taylor: I'll draft the postmortem and include the bisect notes + infra dependency on CUDA.
Maria: Thanks all. Closing channel for alerts; keep the postmortem in #postmortems when ready.
